d.f: DisplayMirrorHost uses a one-way shellStopRequested latch. A later live-mirror START on the same host is not re-armed for STOP, and a failed/null STOP permanently consumes cleanup. Shell DuoShellService independently retains liveMirror until accepted STOP/FORCE_STOP/session rollover.
d.risk: START->STOP->START->DETACH or failed STOP->DETACH can leave shell mirror ownership alive beyond normal host cleanup during the same service lifetime.
d.next: Manager/reviewer should validate generation-aware start-attempt/stop ownership; primary integration only after review.

en: Confirmed source/test finding: the app-side live-mirror STOP latch is one-way. After STOP then a later START on the same host, normal detach can suppress the final STOP; a failed STOP also suppresses retry. The shell retains its own mirror until accepted cleanup. A generation-aware start-attempt/STOP owner fixes the deterministic models while preserving in-flight START cleanup and shell stale-sequence fencing. No production writes.
